page: Amazon Web Services r8a.12xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an AMD EPYC 9R45 processor with 48 dedicated physical cores and 48 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes a cache hierarchy of 48 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core.

In benchmark evaluations, the r8a.12xlarge demonstrates top-tier performance, placing in the top 10% for both single-core and multi-core stress-ng CPU tests, as well as Geekbench and PassMark CPU scores. Its memory subsystem achieves top-tier read-only small block bandwidth and large block write bandwidth, alongside strong large block read-only bandwidth. However, the instance does not include local NVMe storage or dedicated GPU hardware, meaning all storage requirements must be handled over the network via its 22 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

This hardware profile is highly cost-efficient for memory-intensive workloads that do not require local disk storage or GPU acceleration. The combination of high-density DDR5 memory and high-frequency AMD EPYC cores makes the instance particularly suitable for database operations, Redis caching layers, software compilation, and medium-scale language model inference.

Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, it provides 384.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz, translating to 8.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance lacks local storage and dedicated GPUs, relying on a 22 Gbps baseline network bandwidth for external connectivity. In benchmark testing, the r8a.12xlarge delivers top-tier CPU and memory performance, scoring in the top 10% for stress-ng, Geekbench, and PassMark CPU evaluations. It also exhibits high efficiency in database operations, Redis SET transactions, and small-to-medium LLM inference. This profile makes it highly suitable for memory-intensive enterprise workloads, database hosting, and high-throughput caching layers.
